{{Quote|My life spans millennia. Legions have risen to test me&hellip; My ascendance is inevitable. A day, a year, a millennium&mdash;it matters not. I hold the patience of stone and the will of stars. Your striving is insignificant. Let your death be the same.|The Sith Emperor to the Hero of Tython|audio=VitiateSpeech.flac|<ref name="Doomsday">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Doomsday|[[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]}}</ref>}}
'''Tenebrae'''&mdash;known to the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Old Sith Empire]] as '''Darth Vitiate''', his [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] as the '''Sith Emperor, Vitiate''', and his [[Eternal Empire]] as the '''Immortal Emperor''', '''Valkorion'''&mdash;was an ancient [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side]] entity of enormous [[Force power/Legends|power]] who manipulated [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] affairs for nearly 1,500 [[Standard year/Legends|years]].

Born in [[5113 BBY]] as the illegitimate [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] [[Gender/Legends|son]] of [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Dramath]] in the Old Sith Empire, Tenebrae [[Medriaas revolution|carved]] a path of destruction across the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Nathema|Medriaas]], [[Torture/Legends|torturing]] and [[Death/Legends|massacring]] thousands by the age of [[5103 BBY|ten]]. When Dramath confronted him, Tenebrae [[Sever Force/Legends|severed]] his father's power and [[Dramath's holocron|imprisoned]] his spirit for millennia of torment. Eventually, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Marka Ragnos]] recognized Tenebrae's power and christened him as Lord Vitiate—the new ruler of Medriaas. Later historians ascribed the title of Darth to Vitiate during this period, though he himself did not use the title during it. Vitiate renamed the world Nathema and ruled it for the next [[Standard century/Legends|century]], distancing himself from [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] power struggles. Following [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow's]] defeat in the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], Vitiate lured the remaining Sith Lords to Nathema and, in an elaborate [[Ritual of Nathema|ritual]], drained their life essence and that of the entire planet, increasing his powers and prolonging his life.

Shedding his identity as Vitiate, the self-proclaimed [[Sith Emperor/Legends|Sith Emperor]] [[Sith exodus|led]] the scattered Sith survivors to [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] and established a new Sith Empire. As the Empire secretly expanded over the next thousand years, the Emperor discovered the [[Wild Space/Legends|lost]] world of [[Zakuul]] and the [[Eternal Fleet]]—an ancient armada with unmatched technology. Dissatisfied with Sith ideology, the Emperor [[Essence transfer|divided his consciousness]] into a Zakuulan [[warrior]] named [[Valkorion]] and created a vast civilization known as the Eternal Empire. The Emperor desired absolute [[immortality]] to experience the pleasures of life and expand his new creation across galaxies, so he plotted to initiate a war between his Sith Empire and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The deaths caused by the conflict would fuel a new [[Sith Emperor's ritual|ritual]] that would allow him to consume almost everything in the galaxy and become an all-powerful god.

As the Emperor's plans neared completion, he orchestrated the [[Mandalorian Wars]] as a preliminary invasion of the Republic, but two powerful [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]]&mdash;[[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Darth Malak|Malak]]—defeated the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorians]] and [[Mission to Dromund Kaas|tracked down]] his Sith Empire. The Emperor [[Mission to Dromund Kaas|dominated]] their minds, but the pair soon broke free from his [[Mind trick/Legends|control]] and established a [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|separate Sith Empire]], betraying the Emperor—and each other—in the resultant [[Jedi Civil War]] that nearly destroyed the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. A [[Redemption/Legends|redeemed]] Revan waged a mental war against the Emperor, delaying the [[Great Galactic War]] by three centuries. The Sith Empire still [[Sacking of Coruscant|nearly]] conquered the Republic, but Revan further influenced Vitiate—distracted by the births of his three [[Youngling/Legends|children]] to the [[Knights of Zakuul|Zakuul Knight]] [[Senya Tirall]]—to sue for peace instead, prompting a decade-long [[Treaty of Coruscant]].

As hostilities resumed, [[Dark Council]]lor [[Darth Baras]] lured the Emperor to the planet [[Voss]], trapping him in the [[Nightmare Lands|domain]] of the dark-side entity [[Sel-Makor]] until he was rescued by the [[Empire's Wrath|second Emperor's Wrath]]. Freed, the Emperor [[Emperor's ritual crisis|attempted]] to initiate his galaxy-wide ritual, but a powerful Jedi Knight known as the [[Hero of Tython]] thwarted his efforts and destroyed his [[Emperor's Voice (Sith Empire)|host body]] in [[Dromund Kaas operation|battle]] on Dromund Kaas. His wounded spirit went into slumber on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin IV]] until a returned and crazed Revan attempted to resurrect the weakened Emperor to a physical form to permanently destroy him. Although Revan's plans were [[Battle of Yavin 4 (Galactic War)|foiled]] and the Emperor excommunicated by the Empire, Vitiate's spirit fed off the battle and reawakened, then struck against his former Empire and [[Invasion of Ziost|consumed]] the planet [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] to return to full power.

Reassuming the visage of Valkorion, he revealed the Eternal Empire to the galaxy as his twin sons—[[Arcann]] and [[Thexan]]—[[Eternal Empire raids|invaded]] Imperial and Republic space and [[Destruction of Darth Marr's flagship|captured]] a famous champion later known as the [[Alliance Commander|Outlander]] who had opposed him in the Battle of Yavin IV and Invasion of Ziost. Judging the Outlander alone to be a worthy adversary, Valkorion [[Assassination of Valkorion|orchestrated]] his death at the hands of Arcann and embedded his consciousness within the Outlander's mind. The Immortal Emperor counseled and shaped the Outlander into a vessel of supreme power as the champion [[Battle of Odessen|defeated]] Arcann, [[Assault on Odessen|then]] his daughter [[Vaylin]], and [[Battle of Zakuul|disabled]] the Eternal Fleet. Valkorion sought to take over the champion's body and rule the galaxy under the guise of a heroic liberator but, in a final clash of wills, the Outlander and Valkorion's own family reduced the ancient entity into oblivion.

Simultaneous with the expulsion, the former Emperor's Wrath [[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]] and the Jedi Knight [[Kira Carsen]] destroyed the Emperor's original body, dooming his spirit. However, the act released a final, disparate vestige of his essence, [[Tenebrae's curse|imbued into his flesh]] centuries earlier, which soon took hold of [[Grand Master/Legends|Jedi Grand Master]] [[Satele Shan]] and her Jedi followers. Drawing off their memories and power, the imprint slowly reformed itself into a duplicate of Tenebrae and threatened to use Shan as his new host. Many of history's greatest champions, including the Outlander and Revan, along with the souls of all those ever wronged by Tenebrae, joined within Shan's [[mindscape]] and destroyed the Immortal Emperor once and for all.

==Biography==
===Early life and reign===
====Childhood on Medriaas====
{{Quote|Have you ever heard tales of the Emperor's childhood?''"<br />"''I don't even know what planet he's from.''"<br />"''Few people do. He's hidden his past, because if the truth came to light none would follow him.|Darth Nyriss and Lord Scourge|<ref name="Revan" />}}
[[File:Sith_Quad-Sun.svg|thumb|left|Tenebrae was born during the Old Sith Empire, under the rule of Marka Ragnos.]]
The [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith Pureblood]] named Tenebrae was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] in [[5113 BBY]] on [[Nathema|Medriaas]], a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] at the edge of the [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Worlds]]. The illegitimate [[Gender/Legends|son]] of Medriaas' ruler [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Dramath]] and a [[Tenebrae's mother|poor farm woman]], Tenebrae's [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] were said to be as [[Color/Legends|black]] as the void of [[Realspace/Legends|space]], and even as an [[Youngling/Legends|infant]] he showed no emotion, nor did he ever cry. Animals [[Aura of uneasiness|avoided]] him, and his voice seemed to carry power and weight beyond his [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. [[5107 BBY|Around]] the age of six, Tenebrae began to manifest signs of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|strength]] in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], which raised the suspicions of his [[Farm/Legends|farmer]] [[Parent/Legends|stepfather]], as neither he nor his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] were Force-sensitive.<ref name="Revan" />

[[Tenebrae's adoptive father|Tenebrae's stepfather]] confronted his wife in front of a six-year-old Tenebrae, and he proceeded to attack her in anger after she admitted to having had an affair with Lord Dramath. However, Tenebrae [[Consume Essence|fed off]] the man's anger to fuel his own strength in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], and he used his newfound [[Force power/Legends|powers]] to [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetically]] break the farmer's neck. Tenebrae then [[Torture/Legends|tortured]] his mother for [[Standard month/Legends|months]] with the Force before [[Death/Legends|killing]] her for betraying their family, and began to subjugate the other members of [[Tenebrae's village|his village]] with his powers. Over the course of the next [[5103 BBY|four years]], Tenebrae's influence and reputation grew as he conquered neighboring [[City/Legends|villages]] and raised legions of followers. Some followed the child out of fear of his immense power, while others served out of fanatical loyalty. Tenebrae massacred thousands during his rise to power, and tortured people for [[Standard day/Legends|days]] in public executions as he fed off their suffering.<ref name="Revan" />

[[File:Dramath.jpg|thumb|right|Lord Dramath, Tenebrae's father]]
Lord Dramath heard rumors of his son's activities, but because they occurred on the remote<ref name="Revan" /> [[Nathema's northern continent|northern continent]]<ref name="Encyclopedia" />&mdash;and also due to the fact that he had forgotten about his affair with Tenebrae's mother&mdash;the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] believed that the events were of no concern to him. When Tenebrae was around the age of ten, Dramath decided to investigate the rumors of the boy's activities and determine whether he should be killed or become one of his servants. However, the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Lord underestimated his son's abilities; after revealing his true parentage, Tenebrae [[Sever Force/Legends|stripped]] Dramath of his power in the Force and drove the man insane before killing him. Tenebrae then embarked on a [[Medriaas revolution|campaign]] to conquer the rest of Medriaas while his elder half-brother, [[Dramath the Second]], fled the planet to hide from his half-brother on [[Rekkiad]]. It took the child three years to subjugate the world, and any of Lord Dramath's subordinate Sith Lords who attempted to seize the throne fell quickly before Tenebrae's power.<ref name="Revan" />

====Sith Lord of Nathema====
{{Quote|At thirteen he presented himself to Marka Ragnos, the Lord of all Sith and the ruler of the Sith Council. Impressed by the teenager's ambition and power, Marka Ragnos granted him the title of Lord Vitiate.|Darth Nyriss|<ref name="Revan" />}}
[[File:Tenebrae_the_Mortal.jpg|thumb|left|Tenebrae in his original form.]]
After his conquest of Medriaas was complete in [[5100 BBY/Legends|5100 BBY]], Tenebrae traveled to the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire's]] throneworld of [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] and came before [[Marka Ragnos]], the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] and ruler of the [[Sith Council]]. Acknowledging the thirteen-year-old's power, Ragnos granted Tenebrae the right to rule Medriaas as his own and elevated him to the rank of Sith Lord, bestowing the title of Lord Vitiate upon him. Returning to Medriaas, which he renamed [[Nathema]], Vitiate proceeded to build a [[Vitiate's palace|palace]] upon the site of his childhood home and ruled the planet for one hundred years, spending much of that [[Time/Legends|time]] studying the secrets of the dark side.<ref name="Revan" /> Early in his reign, many young Sith flocked to Vitiate, and he taught his new followers to restrain their emotions and draw on their inner anger in order to increase their power.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

When Ragnos' death in [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]] prompted a struggle to determine who would succeed him, Vitiate chose not to involve himself or his world in the battle between the competing Sith Lords [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] and [[Ludo Kressh]]. Vitiate also refrained from participating in the crusade upon which the victorious Sadow embarked against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], instead watching from Nathema as the Sith Empire battled the Republic and their [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] protectors in the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. Vitiate had never participated in any battles or conquests during his reign, and had a reputation of being a reclusive scholar. However, when the Empire met its ultimate defeat in [[Second battle of Korriban|battle]] above the holy tomb world of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], Vitiate put his plans to seize power into action.<ref name="Revan" />

[[File:Tenebrae_Closeup.jpg|thumb|right|Tenebrae sought to ascend beyond mortality through a ritual of his design.]]
Broadcasting speeches across the Empire<ref name="Revan" /> in [[4999 BBY]]<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> describing how the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] would destroy the Empire and massacre its people once they discovered the rest of the Sith, Vitiate stoked the Empire's fears and carefully drove the people into a panic<ref name="Revan" />&mdash;a sensation that only increased when the Republic [[Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion|invaded]] the Empire and destroyed any Sith sacred sites<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> and artifacts<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> it could find<ref name="Timeline 12">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 12: The Great Hyperspace War|int=Timeline 12: The Great Hyperspace War}}</ref> on the orders of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Pultimo]].<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref><ref name="TEGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Assuming a leadership role, Vitiate called all remaining Sith Lords to Nathema in order to aid him in performing a [[Sith Emperor's ritual|ritual]], promising them that it would unleash the full power of the dark side beyond anything they could imagine. At the same time, Vitiate's [[Historian/Legends|historians]] and [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] searched for the location of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]],<ref name="Revan" /> one of the Empire's original colonies<ref name="Book of Sith">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> that Vitiate claimed<ref name="DrewDromund">{{Flickr|url=photos/53636980@N03/6449560549|text=DrewKDromundResponse|author=Drew Karpyshyn|date=2011-12-03|archivedate=20151027060021}}</ref> was the homeworld of the Sith species.<ref name="Revan" />

[[File:Zildrog_from_above.jpg|thumb|left|Zildrog aided Vitiate in destroying all life on Nathema.]]
Just before the other Sith Lords arrived, the researchers finally theorized a [[Kamat Krote|new hyperspace]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|route]] that led back to Dromund Kaas but also prevented the Jedi from following. Three days after the [[Unidentified Sith researcher|lead researcher]] presented the team's findings, Vitiate announced the commencement of his [[Ritual of Nathema|ritual]].<ref name="Revan" /> But when the eight thousand Sith who answered Vitiate's call<ref name="Datacron 31">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 31: The Ritual of Nathema}}</ref> arrived at his palace, he [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|dominated their minds]] and bound their wills to his, forcing the Sith to participate in the ritual.<ref name="Revan" /> The ritual took ten days to perform,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> with the entire planet frozen in the grip of the [[Sith sorcery/Legends|dark-side sorcery]], and upon its completion, all life on the surface of Nathema was annihilated, save for Vitiate. The man [[Force drain/Legends|absorbed]] the [[Living Force/Legends|life force]] of the entire world, stripping the Force from the very fabric of reality on Nathema and gaining both unimaginable power and [[Immortality/Legends|immortality]] as a result. At that moment, the man shed his identity as<ref name="Revan" /> Vitiate<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> and became simply the [[Sith Emperor/Legends|Sith Emperor]], a figure of immense power and wisdom in the eyes of his fellow Sith.<ref name="Revan" />

===Hidden empire===
====Rebuilding an empire====
{{Quote|When I was born, the Emperor was the Empire. Everything existed to feed his whims. He was so far above us. No one, Sith or slave, would have dared even form an opinion about him.|Lord Scourge|audio=ScourgeSpeakOfTheEmperor.flac|<ref name="Dark Offerings">{{TORcite|type=conversation|[[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]]|Dark Offerings}}</ref>}}
[[File:Dromund_Kaas_rally.jpg|thumb|right|The Sith Emperor speaks to his people upon arriving on Dromund Kaas.]]
Blaming the destruction of Nathema on the Jedi,<ref name="Revan" /> the self-declared Emperor<ref name="Datacron 31" /> drove the people of the Empire further into a panic while simultaneously offering them hope. Traveling to Korriban, he promised to lead his people to salvation and safety from the Jedi, and he soon led a great [[Sith exodus|exodus]] from the Sith Worlds into the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Despite knowing the location of Dromund Kaas, the Emperor led his people in a series of blind [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jumps, causing<ref name="Revan" /> the exodus to last for twenty years<ref name="DKHolonet">{{Holonet|planets|dromund-kaas|Dromund Kaas}}</ref> while the Sith people became more and more dependent on his guidance. Finally,<ref name="Revan" /> in [[4980 BBY]],<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> a [[Scout ship/Legends|scout vessel]] under orders of the Emperor located Dromund Kaas. When the [[Starship/Legends|vessel]] returned to the Sith [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]],<ref name="Datacron 32">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 32: Long Exile}}</ref> the Emperor led his people to the long-lost world, and upon reaching the surface he addressed the Sith.<ref name="Datacron 33">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 33: Dromund Kaas}}</ref> Amidst the wild jungles of Dromund Kaas, he declared a [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|new Empire]] that would rise from the ashes of the old,<ref name="Timeline 11">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 11: Rebirth of the Sith Empire|int=Timeline 11: Rebirth of the Sith Empire}}</ref> and offered both the Sith people and their non-Sith servants the chance to build an orderly and powerful society: an Empire that would one day return and gain their revenge upon the Republic.<ref name="Datacron 33" />

[[File:Tenebrae_the_Undying.jpg|thumb|left|Despite achieving effective immortality, Tenebrae still desired far more.]]
The people, who had come to see the Emperor as a kind of [[Deity/Legends|god]], fervently agreed and set to work building their new Empire.<ref name="Revan" /> At first, the Emperor appeared in public often and dictated much of the Empire's policies and actions, but over time he appeared less and less. Not long after arriving on Dromund Kaas, he created the [[Dark Council]]&mdash;a group of twelve Sith Lords who served as the primary ruling body of the Empire&mdash;and the council soon took over much of the day-to-day running of the Empire. The Emperor retreated into seclusion in the newly constructed [[Imperial Citadel (Sith Empire)|Imperial Citadel]] situated in the heart of [[Kaas City]].<ref name="Timeline 11" /> One of his first actions was to select twelve Force-sensitive pureblood Sith to become his [[Hand of the Empire|Hand]]: twelve [[Servant]]s who shared their master's longevity in exchange for allowing him to draw on their strength in order to sustain his powers. The Hand's leader, [[Servant One]], was the first to be bound to the Emperor, while his constant companion [[Servant Two]] gained prophetic powers through a close connection to the Emperor's mind at the expense of his own sanity. The shadowy organization was known only to a few members of the Dark Council throughout the [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], as they operated from obscurity to fulfill their master's will.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

The Emperor spent that time studying even further the mysteries of the Force, unlocking powerful secrets of the dark side.<ref name="The Dark Temple">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Dark Temple}}</ref> In the early years after the arrival on Dromund Kaas,<ref name="Secret Kinds of Darkness">{{TORcite|type=general|Secret Kinds of Darkness|[[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]}}</ref> the Emperor ordered the expansion of the edifice known as the [[Dark Temple]] on the outskirts of Kaas City.<ref name="The Dark Temple" /> An ancient structure that contained the tombs of pre&ndash;Hyperspace War Sith Lords such as [[Aloysius Kallig]],<ref name="Kallig">{{TORcite|type=codex|Kallig}}</ref> the Temple was originally intended as a [[Burial/Legends|burial]] place for the Emperor's enemies, but the Emperor performed powerful dark-side rituals to steal the knowledge and life essences of his enemies in the structure's depths and transformed the area into a [[Vergence/Legends|nexus of dark Force energy]].<ref name="The Dark Temple" /> Those rituals soon also affected Dromund Kaas's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], causing the skies to be filled with perpetual [[Water/Legends|rainstorms]] and lightning.<ref name="Datacron 33" /> One of the [[Sithspawn/Legends|Sithspawn]] created during the rituals escaped deep underground, becoming known as [[Akure]], the Ghost in the Darkness.<ref name="Akure">{{TORcite|type=codex|Akure, the Ghost in the Darkness}}</ref> The Emperor also maintained chambers within the [[Sith Sanctum]], the headquarters of the Sith Order in the Imperial Citadel, though only the Dark Council and the Emperor's personal guard were allowed into the lower levels of the Sanctum.<ref name="The Sith Sanctum">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Sith Sanctum}}</ref>

[[File:Emperor_Kaas_holo.png|thumb|right|The Dark Council handled the day-to-day running of the Empire, but ultimately answered to the Emperor.]]
The [[Imperial Guard]], as those elite [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] who served the Emperor were called, were a group of non-Force-sensitives who served the Emperor with fanatic loyalty and unmatched combat prowess.<ref name="The Imperial Guard Codex">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Imperial Guard}}</ref> Trained in academies on dark-side worlds,<ref name="Imperial Guard Academy">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=codex|Imperial Guard Academy}}</ref> each member of the Guard was brought before the Emperor and bound to his will, making their loyalty absolute. Moreover, the Guard answered only to the Emperor&mdash;the Dark Council had no control over the group's activities, despite the Guard's roles as protectors of the Sith Sanctum. Once the Empire [[Battle of Korriban|reclaimed]] the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] on Korriban over a thousand years later, the Guard also took on the role of guardians for the Academy.<ref name="The Imperial Guard Codex" /> Sometime during his reign, the Emperor also ordered the construction of a [[Emperor's Fortress|personal space station]] in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] of Dromund Kaas, which he used as a temple fortress for [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]] and experimenting with the dark side.<ref name="Emperor's Space Station">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Emperor's Space Station}}</ref>

Around [[4606 BBY]], a Sith named [[Kel'eth Ur]] began to preach Jedi sentiments of peace and serenity while also utilizing the dark side, but the Emperor killed the heretic and sealed his spirit in the Dark Temple&mdash;a fate that befell many of the Emperor's enemies.<ref name="Buried Power">{{TORcite|type=general|Buried Power|[[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]}}</ref> Another Sith Lord named [[Vodal Kressh]] attempted to challenge the Emperor's rule less than four centuries after the Great Hyperspace War, breeding a race of [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] to serve as an [[Tomb Dwellers|army]] on the planet [[Athiss/Legends|Athiss]]. However, Kressh's plans never advanced beyond Athiss, and when the mad Sith died, the Emperor declared Athiss forbidden.<ref name="Athiss">{{TORcite|type=flashpoint|Athiss}}</ref> Several centuries into the Emperor's reign, a Dark Councilor named [[Darth Lokess]] summoned her fellow Council members to a secret meeting in the midst of a violent storm. With an [[Army/Legends|army]] of loyal Sith outside of the meeting ready to kill any Dark Councilor who refused, Lokess described a [[Darth Lokess's conspiracy|plot]] to overthrow the Emperor and lead the Empire into war against the Republic once more&mdash;a plot that all eleven Councilors agreed to join. However, the Emperor learned of the Council's conspiracy and allowed their plans to unfold, but when the twelve ascended the steps of the Citadel to confront him the Emperor delivered his punishment. Lokess' eleven co-conspirators died in a flash of light on the Citadel steps, and Lokess disappeared forever into the bowels of the structure as the Emperor tortured and then finally killed her.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

[[File:DarkCouncilConceptArt-SWTOR.jpg|thumb|left|The Emperor delivers his orders to the Dark Council via hologram.]]
During the Emperor's reign, six Sith Lords&mdash;[[Raptus]], [[Bestia]], [[Brontes]], [[Calphayus]], [[Styrak]], and [[Tyrans]]&mdash;meditated together and developed a powerful variation of [[Battle meditation/Legends|battle meditation]] that allowed them to induce fear in entire armies.<ref name="The Dread Masters">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Dread Masters}}</ref> When Bestia approached the Emperor to share their insights,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> he conferred the title of [[Dread Masters|Dread Master]] upon her and the others for their abilities, and they went on to serve the Emperor for centuries as [[Prophet/Legends|prophets]], [[Advisor/Legends|advisors]], and [[General/Legends|generals]].<ref name="The Dread Masters" />

Another one of the Emperor's experiments in the Dark Temple led to the creation of the [[Ravager (device)|Ravager]], a device that consumed its victims' minds and forced them to reveal their greatest secrets as they died. Not even members of the Dark Council could withstand the Ravager, but the Emperor eventually locked it away in the Dark Temple with other experiments both failed and successful.<ref name="An Ancient Answer">{{TORcite|type=class|Sith Warrior|An Ancient Answer|[[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]]}}</ref> The Dark Temple itself was sealed after a few centuries and remained so for most of the Emperor's reign. Yet, when Kaas City's power grid was expanded into the tunnels beneath the Temple, devices such as the Ravager that were stored in the Temple had the unintentional effect of driving thousands of slaves mad.<ref name="The Dark Temple" />

====Testing the Republic====
{{Quote|They tricked me. We were never meant to win this war. They used me and my people to test the Republic's strength.''"<br />"''Who used you?''"<br />"''The Sith.|Mandalore the Ultimate tells Revan of the Empire with his dying words|<ref name="Revan" />}}
[[File:Mandaloreultimate2.jpg|thumb|right|Mandalore the Ultimate, the Emperor's unknowing pawn]]
At the founding of his Empire, the Emperor had promised to return and destroy the Republic, but over time that goal grew less important to the people of the Empire. However, the Emperor still planned to invade&mdash;but for reasons beyond revenge.<ref name="Revan" /> In his studies, he discovered a way to magnify the ritual he had performed on Nathema so that it would affect the entire [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], and he intended to use war with the Republic as a way to fuel that ritual.<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|An Unthinkable Alliance|the Emperor's Fortress}}</ref> Around [[4043 BBY]],<ref name="The Citadel">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Citadel}}</ref> the Dark Councilors [[Darth Qalar]] and [[Darth Victun]]<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> fought a [[Kaggath (c. 4043 BBY)|vicious]] [[Kaggath]], a Sith ritual duel, that tore apart the Imperial Citadel. When the dust settled, the two were still standing, but the other ten members of the Council combined their powers to obliterate the two.<ref name="The Citadel" /> The Emperor surprised the Dark Council by emerging from seclusion and contributed to the designs for the new Citadel, charging the Sith Lord [[Darth Nostrem]] with completing the building exactly as the plans specified. After the Citadel's completion, the Emperor locked Nostrem in the depths of the Citadel to test the structure's labyrinthine defenses, and was gratified when the Sith Lord perished, unable to find an exit.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

A few decades later, several members of the Dark Council discovered Nathema and learned what the Emperor was truly planning. Those Dark Councilors, among them [[Darth Nyriss]] and [[Darth Xedrix]], began a [[Nathema conspiracy|conspiracy]] to unseat the Emperor and save their Empire and the galaxy from annihilation.<ref name="Revan" /> Not long afterward, around [[3978 BBY]], the Emperor sent a [[Unidentified Sith emissary|Sith Pureblood emissary]] to [[Mandalore the Ultimate]], the leader of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture of warriors. The emissary explained to [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]] that his master had driven a Sith Lord named Dramath the Second into [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]], and convinced the warrior to help him [[Search for Dramath the Second's remains|search]] for [[Dramath the Second's tomb|Dramath's tomb]] on the snowy world of Rekkiad. Breaking into [[Dramath the Second's sarcophagus|Dramath's crypt]] and recovering the Sith Lord's remains for his master, the Sith also told Mandalore of a [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] that the Emperor had received&mdash;one of the Mandalorians crushing the Republic in a glorious victory. However, the Emperor's emissary was also manipulating Mandalore with the power of the dark side, binding the warrior and convincing him to launch a war against the Republic in order to test its strength.<ref name="Revan" />

That conflict, which later become known as the [[Mandalorian Wars]], began [[3976 BBY|two years later]] and raged for a total of sixteen years. The Mandalorians initially had the upper hand until a young [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] known as [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] took command of the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] with his friend and unofficial apprentice [[Darth Malak|Malak]] in [[3962 BBY]]. Under Revan's leadership, the Republic gained more and more ground until they finally forced a confrontation at the [[Battle of Malachor V]] in [[3960 BBY]]. Revan challenged Mandalore the Ultimate to single combat and won, striking down the warrior just as the Jedi's [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] [[Meetra Surik]] activated a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] known as the [[Mass Shadow Generator/Legends|Mass Shadow Generator]]. As Mandalore lay dying, the Emperor's spell was finally broken, and the fallen warrior told his victorious opponent of how he had been manipulated.<ref name="Revan" /> Revan had already encountered Sith ruins on Korriban and Malachor V before the battle<ref name="Chronicles">{{WebCite|url=http://www.gamebanshee.com/starwarskotorii/chronicles.php|text=''Chronicles of the Old Republic'' at Gamebanshee.com|archivedate=20180115001444}}</ref> and unknowingly drew the Emperor's attention in the process, and the Emperor reached out to Revan and Malak. Subtly manipulating them, the Emperor watched<ref name="The Foundry">{{TORcite|type=flashpoint|The Foundry}}</ref> as the pair retraced Mandalore's steps to Rekkiad and discovered the existence of his Empire.<ref name="Revan" />

[[File:RevanMalak-SithEmperor.jpg|thumb|left|Revan and Malak confront the Emperor.]]
Examining a [[Dramath the Second's datacron|datacron]] belonging to the Emperor's half-brother within Dramath's tomb, Revan and Malak discovered the location of Nathema and traveled to the barren world, where they learned the location of Dromund Kaas and witnessed the Emperor's power. Leaving the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic fleet]] that they had brought with them, the pair [[Mission to Dromund Kaas|traveled to Dromund Kaas]] in secret and spent months infiltrating the Imperial Citadel with aid from [[Yarri|one]] of the Imperial Guard&mdash;but what they did not suspect was that each member of the Guard was bound to the Emperor's will and would never betray their master. When Revan and Malak finally infiltrated the Emperor's throne room in an attempt to kill him, the Sith dominated their minds just as he had done so many years ago to the Sith Lords on Nathema.<ref name="Revan" />

Breaking their wills, the Emperor forcibly converted the pair to the dark side<ref name="Revan" /> and declared them [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Revan and his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], Darth Malak. The Emperor sent his new disciples to recover the [[Star Forge]]&mdash;a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] of unimaginable power constructed by the ancient [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]]&mdash;to use in a new war against the Republic.<ref name="T8">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 8: The Jedi Civil War|int=Timeline 8: The Jedi Civil War}}</ref> Publicly, the Emperor informed his people that a pair of [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] had attempted to kill him and that they had been executed as a result. However, the newly converted Sith were stronger than he expected, and they broke free of the Emperor's conditioning.<ref name="Revan" /> Revan decided to declare his own [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]], determined to conquer the Republic<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> and unite it against the Emperor,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> and proceeded to battle the Republic<ref name="KOTOR" /> in what came to be called the [[Jedi Civil War]].<ref name="KOTOR II">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

====Conspiracies====
{{Quote|The Emperor used me as his link to the light side of the Force&mdash;the Jedi Order. Through me, he saw visions. But that same link also gave me influence. I convinced the Emperor peace was in his best interest. Tempered his hate.|Revan|audio=RevanMaelstromEmperor.flac|<ref name="Maelstrom">{{TORcite|type=flashpoint|Maelstrom Prison}}</ref>}}
[[File:Sith_Emperor.jpg|thumb|right|The Sith Emperor personally intervened in Nyriss' affairs, disrupting her plans.]]
Revan was eventually betrayed by his apprentice during a [[Capture of Darth Revan|Jedi attempt to capture him]], and Malak seized control of their Empire, while Revan's mind was [[Amnesia/Legends|wiped clean]] by the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]]. Revan went on to destroy the very Empire he had created and [[Battle of Rakata Prime|defeated]] Malak aboard the Star Forge,<ref name="KOTOR" /> but in the years after the war he was plagued by memories of Dromund Kaas. At the same time, the conspirators against the Emperor began to suspect they were on the verge of being discovered. Therefore, Darth Nyriss arranged for several [[Assassination attempts on Darth Nyriss|assassination attempts against herself]] in [[3954 BBY]] as a way of framing the aged [[Human/Legends|Human]] Darth Xedrix. However, the Emperor interfered with her plans by "suggesting" that she bring in outside assistance in the form of the Sith Lord [[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]].<ref name="Revan" />

Nyriss led Scourge through a series of elaborate tests and deceptions as part of his investigations, culminating with Scourge's murder of Xedrix. At that point, Nyriss revealed the conspiracy to Scourge, and in order to convince him to join their cause, she took him to Nathema. However, at the same time Revan had been retracing his steps with the help of his ally [[Canderous Ordo]] on Rekkiad. Discovering the existence of the Empire and the location of Nathema, Revan traveled there with his [[Droid/Legends|droid]] companion [[T3-M4]] aboard their [[Dynamic-class freighter/Legends|ship]], the ''[[Ebon Hawk]]''. Both Sith and Jedi arrived simultaneously, though Revan did not detect Nyriss' ship at first. The Dark Councilor and Scourge, now entirely believing in the conspiracy's cause, shot down the ''Ebon Hawk'' and captured the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]], whom Nyriss identified as Revan.<ref name="Revan" />

Revan was held in [[Prisoner/Legends|captivity]] by Nyriss for four years, tortured under the direction of Scourge, until Revan's former lieutenant Meetra Surik&mdash;better known as the Jedi Exile&mdash;followed her friend's trail to Dromund Kaas with T3-M4 in [[3950 BBY]]. Scourge, who had come to trust Revan during the last four years, decided to join forces with him and Surik to destroy the Emperor. As part of their plan, Scourge approached the Emperor and exposed Nyriss' conspiracy, careful to exclude his role in the plot, so that the Emperor would take action against the Dark Councilor. However, the Emperor did not act as Scourge expected: instead of simply eliminating the conspirators, the Emperor decided to [[Purge of the Dark Council|purge]] the entire Dark Council.<ref name="Revan" />

[[File:RevanconfrontsSithEmperor.jpg|thumb|left|Revan attacks the Emperor.]]
The Emperor summoned nine members of the Council, seven of whom were loyal and two who were conspirators, to his chambers in the Citadel and killed them. Only [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] later, he dispatched the Imperial Guard to destroy the estates of the three remaining Councilors, whom he had not expected to answer his summons on account of their treachery, with the full force of the [[Imperial Military (Sith Empire)|Imperial Military]]. The three members of the Dark Council were caught entirely by surprise, and the Guard decimated their entire power bases as well as the power bases of the other two conspirators. However, Revan was freed by Scourge and Surik during the chaos, and the trio prepared to end the threat that the Emperor posed once and for all. Revan, Scourge, Surik, and T3-M4 [[Attack on the Sith Emperor|infiltrated]] the Imperial Citadel and fought their way past the Imperial Guard, facing the Emperor in his throne room. Revan and his [[Cleaning droid/Legends|utility droid]] charged their enemy, causing the Emperor to [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Push|blast]] the Jedi Master with the Force. Advancing on his opponent, the Sith attempted to dominate Revan's mind once again, but the Jedi opened himself to both the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] and dark sides to unleash the Force in its purest form, an attack that sent the Emperor flying backward.<ref name="Revan" />

When Revan attempted to charge the distracted Emperor, the Sith unleashed a blast of [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] that sent him screaming to the floor, and [[Force Destruction|blasted]] T3-M4 into shrapnel when the droid attacked with his [[Flamethrower/Legends|flamethrower]]. Picking up his fallen foe's [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], the Emperor attempted to kill Revan with the weapon but was stopped when Surik knocked it out of the Sith's hands with her own [[Meetra Surik's first lightsaber|weapon]]. Faced by Surik, Revan, and Scourge, the Emperor expressed his disappointment with the latter&mdash;who was suddenly overcome with visions of the future. Realizing that it was not their destiny to defeat the Emperor, but was in fact the fate of another, Scourge chose to betray his allies by stabbing Surik in the back and distracting Revan enough for the Emperor to blast the Jedi Master with more lightning.<ref name="Revan" />

Testing Scourge's loyalty, the Emperor ordered him to kill Revan, but stopped him just before the lightsaber reached its mark. The Emperor decided to imprison Revan, prolonging his life indefinitely through a combination of [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]] and technology, and placing him in a specially constructed [[Prison/Legends|prison]] in the heart of the impossible-to-navigate [[Maelstrom Nebula/Legends|Maelstrom Nebula]]. Scourge, who claimed to have deceived the two Jedi in order to bring them before the Emperor, was rewarded with the position of [[Emperor's Wrath]], his personal enforcer, and the same immortality that Revan received. Surik's [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] survived the death of her body, however, and remained faithfully at her friend's side while the Emperor fed off Revan's strength and knowledge. With the strength Surik lent him, Revan fought the Emperor's control and even influenced the Emperor in return,<ref name="Revan" /> tempering the Sith leader's desire to restart war and postponing the renewal of conflict with the Republic for almost three centuries.<ref name="Maelstrom" />

===Return to the known galaxy===
====Final preparations and a new empire====
{{Quote|The Emperor has manipulated events for centuries toward one goal: performing an even greater ritual that will destroy this galaxy.|Lord Scourge|audio=ScourgeEmperorRitual.flac|<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance" />}}
[[File:Sithemperorbloodoftheempire.jpg|thumb|right|The Emperor's Voice during the early Great Galactic War]]
Despite Revan's influence, the Emperor's will could not be stopped, only slowed. Over the next 200 years, the Emperor advanced his plans for a new invasion. However, Revan's plot and near-successful assassination attempt unsettled the Emperor immensely, and as a result, the Empire's ruler delved into further studies of the dark side. In his studies, the Emperor discovered the rare technique of [[essence transfer]] to preserve his physical form from harm.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> Using the technique to transfer his life force between bodies, he created the position of [[Emperor's Voice (Sith Empire)|Emperor's Voice]]&mdash;the host body of his consciousness and the ultimate extension of his will. Throughout the next three centuries, the Emperor utilized many Voices<ref name="The Voice of the Emperor" /> as the ravaging effects of the dark side took their toll upon the host bodies.<ref name="Dark Empire">[[Dark Empire 5|''Dark Empire'' 5]]</ref> Those hosts varied widely, including the bodies of a [[Unidentified Emperor's Voice (Human female)|young Human female]] and an [[Unidentified Emperor's Voice (Sith Pureblood)|elderly Sith Pureblood]], but they always possessed the same emotionless, cold male voice.<ref name="The Voice of the Emperor" /> The Emperor's mental link with Revan also enabled the Emperor to torture the captured Force user, and both the Emperor and the Dread Masters spent centuries attacking Revan's mind, trying to break him and turn him to the dark side once more. Revan resisted, but the stress caused his mind to fracture, and he separated himself from the pain, concentrating only on the Force.<ref name="The Enemy Within">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=general|The Enemy Within|[[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]}}</ref>

[[File:Immortal_Emperor_Valkorion.jpg|thumb|left|Vitiate as Immortal Emperor Valkorion]]
Around this time, the Emperor decided that he was tired of the galaxy as it existed, and of the limits that Sith teachings and his empire placed upon him. Resolving to free himself of such restraints,<ref name="KOTFE 2">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=2}}</ref> Vitiate heard rumors of an ancient and unstoppable fleet of warships operated by sentient droids that had nearly wiped out all of [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].<ref name="Eternal Fleet">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|The Eternal Fleet}}</ref> A powerful ship known as the [[Gravestone]] purportedly stopped the entire "[[Eternal Fleet]]" at a backwater planet called [[Zakuul]],<ref name="Gravestone">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|The Gravestone}}</ref> and so Vitiate chose Zakuul as the world upon which he would build a new empire&mdash;a truly [[Eternal Empire]].<ref name="Eternal Fleet" /> Vitiate took on a Human male body as a new Voice that went by the name "[[Valkorion]]," though he split his mind and energy between the Valkorion body and the numerous Voices that oversaw the Sith Empire's march to war.<ref name="Valkorion">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|Valkorion}}</ref> Zakuul's native Humans were a superstitious and nihilistic people who worshipped the ruthless [[Six Gods|Old Gods]], and so "Valkorion" claimed to be the [[Demon Savior]] of Zakuulan prophecy&mdash;an immortal god of gods who would topple [[Izax]] the Ultimate Devourer and the rest of the Old Gods, and thus usher in a new age.<ref name="Old Ways">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|The Old Ways of Zakuul}}</ref>

[[File:Valkorion_the_Immortal_Emperor.jpg|thumb|right|Unlike his other Voices, Vitiate fully subdued and suppressed the personality of the original Valkorion.]]
Uniting the nomadic tribes of Zakuul, Valkorion declared himself the Immortal Emperor of a new Eternal Empire,<ref name="Knights of Zakuul">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|Knights of Zakuul}}</ref> and established a city amid the swamps as he accelerated the Zakuulans' technological advancement. However, the city was not grand enough for Valkorion, and his rapidly growing civilization became based in the [[Spire (Zakuul)|Spire]], a golden metropolis that sprawled outwards from atop the [[Old World]], as the first city became known.<ref name="KOTFE 7">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=7}}</ref> He repurposed the three tribal leadership roles&mdash;[[Matriarch (Zakuul)|Matriarch]], [[Champion (Zakuul)|Champion]], and [[High Shaman]]&mdash;into the [[Knights of Zakuul]], an order of Force users who were considered protectors of the people and were fanatical in their devotion to their Immortal Emperor.<ref name="Knights of Zakuul" /> A subgroup of the Knights, the [[Scions of Zakuul]], specialized in seeing the future and were obsessed with the idea of fate.<ref name="Scions">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|Scions of Zakuul}}</ref>

[[File:Valkorion_the_Cunning.jpg|thumb|left|As Valkorion, Tenebrae spent centuries cultivating an entirely new society, separate from the larger galaxy.]]
Valkorion used this to his advantage, using the Scions' Force visions to find the dormant fleet.<ref name="Eternal Fleet" /> To control the fleet, he gathered Zakuul's greatest minds and set them to work building the [[Eternal Throne]]: a throne in the [[Skyscraper/Legends|starscraper]] that topped the Spire whose technology gave the Immortal Emperor control over<ref name="Eternal Throne">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|The Eternal Throne}}</ref> the [[GEMINI]] units that operated the fleet.<ref name="Eternal Fleet" /> The throne took generations to complete, finishing around two centuries after the Jedi Civil War,<ref name="Eternal Throne" /> but for some reason Valkorion kept the Eternal Fleet within the Unknown Regions for the centuries that followed.<ref name="KOTFE 4">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=4}}</ref>

Meanwhile, the Emperor's plans for war in the greater galaxy continued, as he sought to use such a conflict to fuel himself as he did on Nathema.<ref name="Confederacy">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=general|Confederacy|[[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]}}</ref> The Force-sensitive [[Ovair family]] was installed in the Jedi Order at his request, giving him a family line of Sith [[Spy/Legends|spies]] within the ranks of his enemies. Around [[3756 BBY]], the Emperor became aware of the [[Naga Sadow's tomb|tomb]] of Naga Sadow on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. Viewing Sadow's powers as a potential threat to his planned invasion and his position as ruler of the Sith, the Emperor ordered his agent, Jedi Master [[Barel Ovair]], to eliminate any remnant of the Sith's spirit. Ovair and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Eison Gynt]] traveled to the moon on behalf of the Jedi Order with the purpose of ridding it of dark-side energies, but the pair were attacked on their [[Mission to Yavin 4|mission]] by the descendants of Sadow's [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors. Ovair eventually returned to the Republic [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] later without his Padawan, but Sadow possessed Gynt and resurfaced several years later in a [[Duel on Coruscant (Inter–Sith Wars Period)|failed attempt]] to kill the undercover Sith. The [[Jedi historian]] [[Gnost-Dural]] deduced centuries later that Ovair had been in fact been targeted by Sadow's spirit because he was a servant of the Sith Emperor, and that the infiltrator had used Gynt to draw out and eliminate Sadow's spirit before the Empire invaded.<ref name="Timeline 7">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 7: Peace for the Republic?|int=Timeline 7: Peace for the Republic?}}</ref>

With Naga Sadow's spirit vanquished, the Emperor took Yavin 4 for his own, and established the [[Imperial Guard Academy]]<ref name="Imperial Guard Academy" /> there to guard the [[Temple of Sacrifice]], an ancient Sith edifice that held a powerful Sith artifact. With the accompanying ritual, the artifact would allow the Emperor to absorb all life on the moon, and thus it was kept as a failsafe plan in case the Voice was slain.<ref name="The Devoted Ones">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=general|The Devoted Ones|Yavin 4}}</ref> One of the Imperial Guardsmen who underwent training at Yavin 4 was the hardened slave [[Iven]], whose unchecked, murderous rage allowed him to resist the Emperor's indoctrination process longer than any other Guardsman&mdash;but his resistance caused his mind to snap. Now permanently in the Emperor's thrall, the insane Iven became the most ruthless and devoted of the Emperor's Guard.<ref name="Commandant Iven">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=codex|Commandant Iven}}</ref>

Around the turn of the thirteenth century of his rule, the Emperor became the [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]] of [[Exal Kressh]], a hybrid Human&ndash;Sith descendant of Ludo Kressh.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 1" /> He also began to experiment with learning and combining different Force techniques<ref name="Blood of the Empire 2">''[[The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire Act 2: The Broken World]]''</ref> in an effort to extend his reach and sight beyond the capabilities of his Hand alone.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> During her apprenticeship, Kressh was sent to a [[Ambrian monastery|monastery]] on [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]], where the Emperor experimented on her and prepared to make her a vessel for his mind.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 2" /> He also spent decades installing infiltrators in positions of power throughout the galaxy.<ref name="Book of Sith" /> Throughout all of this, Vitiate secretly maintained two Voices: the Human Valkorion body in the Unknown Regions, and the various bodies that served as the Voice in the Sith Empire.<ref name="KOTFE 1" />

====A renewed war====
{{Quote|The execution of the Emperor's brilliant strategy was flawless. Survival was the best the Republic could hope for.|Jedi Master Gnost-Dural|audio=EmperorPlan.flac|<ref name="Timeline 5">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 5: The Battle of Bothawui|int=Timeline 5: The Battle of Bothawui}}</ref>}}
[[File:Exel_Kressh.jpg|thumb|right|Exal Kressh, the Emperor's apprentice]]
Finally, in [[3681 BBY]], the Emperor announced that the Sith Empire would return to the known galaxy and launch its assault on the Republic.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> His meticulously calculated plans, in collaboration with the Imperial Military, resulted in a series of victories against the Republic in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], including the successful [[Assault on the Aparo sector|capture]] of the [[Aparo sector/Legends|Aparo sector]]<ref name="Timeline 6">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 6: Onslaught of the Sith Empire|int=Timeline 6: Onslaught of the Sith Empire}}</ref> following his activation of his agents in the governments of [[Ruuria/Legends|Ruuria]], [[Sernpidal/Legends|Sernpidal]], and [[Belkadan/Legends|Belkadan]].<ref name="Book of Sith" /> As the [[Imperial Army (Sith Empire)|Imperial Army]] and [[Imperial Navy (Sith Empire)|Imperial Navy]] [[Battle of Sluis Van (Great Galactic War)|conquered]] planets such as [[Sluis Van/Legends|Sluis Van]], Imperial [[Troop/Legends|troops]] massacred anyone who would not swear loyalty to their new Emperor, and [[Republic trooper|troopers]] of the Republic Military were simply killed on sight.<ref name="Gnost">[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'']]</ref>

By the [[3678 BBY|third year]] of the [[Great Galactic War]], as the conflict soon became known, the Emperor was advancing his plans to spread his influence throughout the galaxy. Through centuries of experimentation, he was developing a combination of mental domination and transference of his consciousness that would allow him to create his "[[Children of the Emperor|Children]]"&mdash;the ultimate agents of his will, as the Children would be extensions of his mind who would only be aware of their true allegiance when he allowed them to be. In the depths of the Sith Academy on the recently reclaimed Korriban, the Emperor's servants were completing the machines and rituals necessary for the process, and his servants were scouring the galaxy for young initiates.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 3">''[[The Old Republic, Blood of the Empire Act 3: Burn the Future]]''</ref> To that end, he dispatched Kressh to the ash world of [[Lenico IV]] to learn from [[Ortolan/Legends|Ortolan]] colonists. The colonists' legends spoke of [[Shaman/Legends|shamans]] who lived on through their descendants, something that was of interest to the Emperor's plans for his Children.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 2" />

[[Massacre on Lenico IV|Massacring]] the Ortolan colonists on her master's orders after her mission was complete, Kressh returned to the Empire and was sent to the [[Kathol Rift/Legends|Kathol Rift]]. However, the Ortolans' stories opened Kressh's eyes, and she realized that the Emperor intended to hollow out her mind and possess her as the first of his Children.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 2" /> Fleeing her duties and traveling into Republic space, she began to feed the Republic information, and then locked herself in stasis aboard the medical space station [[Lenico Colony Blue|Colony Blue]] above Lenico, where the Emperor could only sense her [[Dream/Legends|dreams]]. Not long after her betrayal, the Emperor witnessed a vision of the Sith Lord [[Nankrang]] emerging [[Engagement in the Mid Rim|victorious]] over the Jedi in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]], and he personally chose the banner that the Sith Lord's forces would carry into battle.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 1" />

Desiring to bring his wayward apprentice back under his control, the Emperor ordered the Dark Council to retrieve her, and the Council summoned the Sith apprentice [[Darth Thanaton|Teneb Kel]] to Dromund Kaas. There, Kel was brought before the Emperor&mdash;whose current Voice was a [[Unidentified Human Emperor's Voice (3678 BBY)|young Human male]]&mdash;and ordered to find Kressh in the [[Lenico system/Legends|Lenico system]].<ref name="Blood of the Empire 1" /> The [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith assassin]] Kel chased Kressh across the galaxy, encountering her aboard Lenico Colony Blue, but failing to capture her until he finally [[Battle over Korriban|killed her]], in the depths of the Sith Academy on Korriban, where he stopped her from destroying the Emperor's plans. After he learned why Kressh had fled the Emperor, Kel returned to the Council and demanded to be elevated to Lordship in exchange for the information. The Council accepted and granted Kel the title of Darth Thanaton, and in return they learned of the existence of the Children of the Emperor.<ref name="Blood of the Empire 3" /> In revenge for his apprentice's betrayal, the Emperor declared the very name Kressh an abomination and ordered all evidence of the family line across the Empire be destroyed. The [[Kressh family]] was obliterated from the history and fabric of the Empire, ensuring that the relatives of the Emperor's rebellious apprentice would never rise up against him.<ref name="The Obliteration of Kressh">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Obliteration of Kressh}}</ref>

[[File:ChildOfTheEmperorPreparation-BurnTheFuture.png|thumb|left|A child is prepared for the Emperor's rituals in the depths of the Sith Academy.]]
At the orders of the Emperor, Force-sensitive children of many [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="Children of the Emperor">{{TORcite|type=codex|Children of the Emperor}}</ref> were taken from their families and entered in a special group at the Sith Academy.<ref name="The Defector">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|The Defector|the Abandoned Mining Facility}}</ref> Those children came from many different places and backgrounds: [[Syo Bakarn]] was a member of a [[Bakarn family|noble house]] on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]],<ref name="Old Blood">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|Old Blood|[[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]}}</ref> [[Augin Blaesus]] was from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Erigorm]],<ref name="To Serve the King">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|To Serve the King|[[Waypoint Station Three]]}}</ref> and [[Kira Carsen]] was born on Dromund Kaas.<ref name="The Defector" /> At different points during their training, each of the children spent weeks undergoing various rituals and processes in the depths of the Academy,<ref name="Blood of the Empire 3" /> culminating in an audience with the Emperor where they were infused with the Emperor's strength and bound to his mind and will. Bakarn became the [[Emperor's First Son]], shielding the other Children from detection while also serving on the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]], and the Children were sent out into the galaxy as the ultimate undercover agents.<ref name="Chaos and Harmony">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|Chaos and Harmony|[[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]}}</ref>

Unless the Emperor willed it, his Children [[Sleeper agent/Legends|knew nothing]] of their connection to the Sith or even their Force-sensitivity, and they became high-ranking individuals with influence across the galaxy. Some were planetary representatives,<ref name="To Serve the King" /> others members of the Republic Military,<ref name="Category Ten">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|Category Ten|[[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]]}}</ref> and some even became members of the Jedi Order.<ref name="Chaos and Harmony" /> Kira Carsen escaped Imperial space before the process could be completed when the ten-year-old realized what the Emperor was doing to her, though she would eventually draw the Emperor's attention during her time as a member of the Jedi Order.<ref name="The Defector" />

[[File:Sith_Emperor_plotting.png|thumb|right|The Great Galactic War marked the first time in centuries that the Emperor personally directed the Empire's actions.]]
As the war continued, the Empire scored victory after victory against an unprepared Republic, claiming worlds such as [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] and [[Agamar/Legends|Agamar]] in their second main offensive.<ref name="The Sith Empire">{{Holonet|allegiances|sith-empire|The Sith Empire}}</ref> The Imperial [[Third battle of the Seswenna sector|capture]] of the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]] in [[3671 BBY]] was countered when the Republic won a resounding victory at the [[First Battle of Bothawui]], and the heroic last stand of Jedi Master [[Belth Allusis]] and his men at the [[Battle of Bothawui (Second; Great Galactic War)|second battle]] inspired the Republic to fight back against the seemingly unstoppable Imperial advance.<ref name="Timeline 5" /> Only a [[3668 BBY|few years later]], a Republic strike team led by Jedi Knight [[Jaric Kaedan]] [[Capture of the Dread Masters|captured the Dread Masters]], depriving him of his advisors' powerful fear-inducing battle meditation abilities. A further blow to the Imperial war effort came when a much smaller [[Republic Army|Republic force]] [[Ground warfare/Legends|defeated]] the Imperial invasion forces at the [[Battle of Alderaan]] in [[3667 BBY]], but the Republic's resurgence was broken with the disastrous [[Space warfare/Legends|naval conflict]] known as the [[Battle of Hoth (Great Galactic War)|Battle of Hoth]] in [[3665 BBY]].<ref name="Gnost" />

[[File:Young_Valkorion.png|thumb|left|Valkorion observes his two newborn sons in their cribs.]]
With the offensive going well once more, the Emperor became distracted by something else in the Unknown Regions&mdash;around that time, a young Knight named [[Senya Tirall]] joined Valkorion's elite guard, and the Immortal Emperor had begun to phase out Humans from the Eternal Empire's military in favor of droids such as the new [[Skytrooper]] battle droid. Tirall spoke out against the change, catching Valkorion's attention; her willingness to speak her mind earned her a permanent posting to Valkorion's elite guard, and the two began a secret affair two years later. They were happy for a time until Tirall bore twin sons, [[Arcann]] and [[Thexan]]. As they grew, the two boys adored their father and were indifferent to their mother's affections, but Valkorion himself grew increasingly distant as the war against the Republic drew his attention. The Valkorion body barely acknowledged the presence of his family for weeks at a time as he concentrated his power and focus elsewhere.<ref name="KOTFE 7" /> 

[[File:Valkorion_ignores_his_sons.png|thumb|right|Valkorion denies the attention to his sons, Arcann and Thexan.]]
By [[3660 BBY]], the Emperor was growing restless, and the [[Battle on the Hydian Way|breaking]] of the Imperial-sponsored Mandalorian [[Blockade of the Hydian Way|blockade]] of the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] did nothing to help the chances of ending the war.<ref name="Timeline 2">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 2: The Mandalorian Blockade is Broken|int=Timeline 2: The Mandalorian Blockade is Broken}}</ref> Not long after the [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]], a resilient Republic [[Battle of Ziost|struck at Ziost]], although the Empire eventually defeated the attackers in a battle lasting more than a month. The Republic assault was foiled again at the subsequent [[Battle of Ashas Ree]], but the Republic's success at the earlier [[Battle of Ord Radama]] angered the Emperor enough to demand that the Empire retake the world. Spurred on by their Lord's command, Lords [[Darth Malgus]] and [[Darth Angral]] led Imperial forces to a costly victory in the [[Reconquest of Ord Radama]].<ref name="Book of Sith" />

[[File:Vaylin_Valkorion_and_Senya.jpg|thumb|left|Valkorion observes his daughter Vaylin's training incident.]]
As the war neared the end of its third decade, Revan's influence on the Emperor<ref name="Maelstrom" /> resulted in something that many Sith found surprising: plans for peace.<ref name="Threat of Peace 1">''[[The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 1: Treaty of Coruscant]]''</ref> Both the Emperor and the Dark Council were desperate for an end to the brutal war, which as it dragged on was forcing the Empire to strip entire worlds of their resources and peoples to fuel the Imperial war machine.<ref name="Lost Suns 1">[[The Old Republic — The Lost Suns 1|''The Old Republic — The Lost Suns'' 1]]</ref> Around the same time, Tirall gave birth to a daughter she named [[Vaylin]], but the child inherited her father's immense power&mdash;she made furniture move while still in the womb, and tore apart droids as a toddler. Tirall was horrified when her daughter crippled a guard after dropping a ball she had tossed, and went to Valkorion for help.<ref name="KOTFE 7" /> Though distracted, Valkorion had been paying some attention to his children, and the similarities between himself and his favorite child both pleased and frightened the Sith entity.<ref name="Vaylin">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|Vaylin}}</ref>

[[File:Valkorion_the_Bad_Father.jpg|thumb|right|Valkorion kept himself emotionally closed from his children.]]
When Tirall came to him and begged him to help their daughter, Valkorion's "solution" was to install mental blocks that separated Vaylin from most of her powers and suppressed her violent and sociopathic tendencies, but also damaged her personality. Tirall attempted to flee with her children, but they rejected her concerns and scorned her affections, so a broken-hearted Tirall returned to service in the enforcement division of the Knights on the outer fringes of the Empire, never to speak with Valkorion again.<ref name="KOTFE 7" /> In her absence, Valkorion remained emotionally distant from his children, teaching them his philosophy that one could achieve anything if they were willing to sacrifice, and changing their guards regularly to prevent them from becoming attached. Doing so reminded his children that while the Knights of Zakuul served his children, the Knights considered the three of them to be merely extensions of Valkorion's will.<ref name="Brothers">{{TORweb|url=info/news/blog/20150728|text="Brothers"|int=Brothers (short story)}}</ref> However, he later came to regret his indifference towards Tirall, considering his letting her leave to be a mistake.<ref name="KOTFE 2" />

[[File:Valkorion_welcomes_Vaylin.jpg|thumb|left|Valkorion welcomes Vaylin after her return from Nathema.]]
While some of the seven surviving Dark Councilors wanted to continue the war, the Emperor's plans were put in motion around [[3654 BBY]] after he gave them consolation: each of the seven would receive their own [[Star system/Legends|star system]] from the Republic as part of the upcoming treaty. At the Emperor's request, the Sith Lord [[Darth Baras]] led a delegation to approach the Republic with an offer of peace in [[3653 BBY]]. Yet while [[Alderaan peace conference|negotiations]] were underway on the planet [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], an armada under Darth Angral [[Sacking of Coruscant|attacked]] the Republic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and held it captive. Using Coruscant as a bargaining chip, the Empire forced the Republic to sign the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] and end the Great Galactic War.<ref name="Threat of Peace 1" /> The Treaty forced the Republic to immediately withdraw all of its military forces from battlefields across the galaxy and redrew the galactic boundaries, effectively granting the Empire control of those parts of the galaxy that lay to the west and north of the Core as well as north of the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]].<ref name="Timeline 1">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant|int=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant}}</ref> However, after the Treaty's completion, the Emperor retreated back into seclusion and left the Empire under the control of the Dark Council.<ref name="The Sith Empire" />

====Cold War====
{{Quote|I see futures in you. Futures I will not allow. Your future ends here.|The Emperor, to the Jedi Knight later known as the Hero of Tython|audio=VitiateFutures.flac|<ref name="Fate of the Jedi">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Fate of the Jedi|the ''Oppressor''}}</ref>}}
[[File:Voss_Mystic.jpg|thumb|right|The Emperor took an interest in the Voss after learning of their prophetic abilities.]]
The signing of the treaty began a period that soon came to be called the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], where both the Empire and the Republic rebuilt their strength and engaged in various minor proxy engagements to test their enemy's readiness. The Emperor retained an iron grip on the hearts and minds of his people despite his seemingly apathetic role in governing them, and the Dark Council continued their typical power plays and maneuvering as they ran the Empire.<ref name="Fatal Alliance">''[[The Old Republic: Fatal Alliance]]''</ref> Around [[3645 BBY]],<ref name="Voss-Date">{{TORcite|type=class|Imperial Agent|Paying Respects|[[Voss]]}} establishes that the [[Bas-Ton (imposter)|impostor Bas-Ton]] has been on [[Voss]] for five years, and he was sent there to infiltrate [[Voss (species)|Voss]] society after the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire's]] [[Imperial Attack on Voss|invasion]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] failed. Additionally, ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]'' places the events of Act III, which include Voss, in approximately [[3640 BBY]]; thus, the invasion of Voss occurred in approximately [[3645 BBY]]. Finally, {{TORcite|type=class|Sith Warrior|Request An Audience|[[Voss]]}} establishes that the [[Unidentified Emperor's Voice (Voss)|Voss host]] for the Emperor was taken simultaneously with the invasion.</ref> a new world named [[Voss]] was discovered by the Empire, and reports delivered by Darth Baras on the Force-sensitive [[Voss (species)|Voss]] species intrigued the Emperor.<ref name="Request An Audience">{{TORcite|type=class|Sith Warrior|Request An Audience|[[Voss]]}}</ref> The species was ruled by a group of [[Voss Mystics|Mystics]] whose prophecies were always accurate,<ref name="Mystics">{{TORcite|type=codex|Voss Mystics}}</ref> and the Emperor desired to have one of them as his Voice. As a result, an Imperial force [[Imperial Attack on Voss|attacked the planet]] while the Emperor's Hand kidnapped a [[Unidentified Emperor's Voice (Voss)|Mystic]] from the surface,<ref name="Request An Audience" /> although the attacking force was destroyed by the machinations of the [[Star Cabal]].<ref name="Hidden Throne">{{TORcite|type=class|Imperial Agent|The Hidden Throne|[[Isen IV|Isen Four]]}} establishes that [[Imperial Intelligence (Sith Empire)|Imperial Intelligence]] investigated all occurrences of [[Starship/Legends|starships]] spontaneously exploding via [[Hunter (Star Cabal)|Hunter's]] override technology in the last five [[Standard year/Legends|years]], and this led [[Cipher Nine]] to the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]] and [[Voss]]. Additionally, the [[Star Cabal]] sent the [[Albathius|Shining Man]] to Voss in the aftermath of the [[Invasion of Voss|invasion]], as they wished to prevent the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] and [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] from controlling the world. Thus, it can be determined that the destruction of the ships during the Voss invasion was also caused by the Star Cabal.</ref> The Emperor studied his captive's abilities throughout the Cold War, utilizing the Voss's prophetic powers to see visions of the future.<ref name="Request An Audience" />

A decade after the Treaty of Coruscant,<ref name="Time">{{TOR_dates|1}}</ref> the [[Hero of Tython|former apprentice]] of Jedi Master [[Orgus Din]] drew the ire of Darth Angral when the Jedi Knight [[Duel in the Jedi Temple ruins|killed]] the Sith's son [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis]] on Coruscant.<ref name="Race to the Ruins">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Race to the Ruins|[[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]}}</ref> Driven mad with grief, Angral [[Desolator crisis|waged war]] against the Republic using stolen superweapons, which caused the Emperor to take an interest in the subject of Angral's wrath. When Angral encountered the Knight's apprentice Kira Carsen on the planet [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]], the Sith Lord was surprised to learn that the Padawan was a former Child, and he informed the Emperor almost immediately. Desiring to control Carsen once again, the Emperor sent her former fellow Child [[Valis]] to retrieve her.<ref name="The Defector" />

{{GameLS}}
On the Emperor's orders, Valis lured Carsen and her Master to an [[Czerka asteroid mining facility|abandoned mining facility]] and [[Duel at the Czerka mining facility|battled the pair]] in an attempt to recapture Carsen.<ref name="The Defector" /> When Carsen and the Knight finally [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|faced]] Angral aboard his [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] [[Oppressor (Harrower-class)|''Oppressor'']], the Emperor chose that moment to take control of her. On the Emperor's orders, Angral [[Battle of the Oppressor|battled]] the Knight to the death, and the Emperor took full control of Carsen when Angral [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|fell]] to the Jedi's blade. However, with help from her Master, Carsen summoned a [[wall of light]] to permanently sever her connection to the Emperor. The loss of Carsen angered the Emperor, but he soon became suspicious of the Knight, who became known as the Hero of [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] after the battle with Angral,<ref name="Fate of the Jedi" /> and grew wary of the Jedi's power<ref name="The Emperor's Wrath">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|The Emperor's Wrath|[[Quesh]]}}</ref> over the next year.<ref name="Time2">{{TOR_dates|2}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

===A new war===
====The Jedi threat====
{{Quote|You are mine. Servants. Slaves. Weapons. And you will obey&hellip;|The Emperor takes control of the Jedi strike team|<ref name="Descent">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Descent|the Emperor's Fortress}}</ref>}}
[[File:EmperorsFortress-SWTOR.png|thumb|left|The Emperor's ancient space station above Dromund Kaas]]
In [[3642 BBY]],<ref name="Annihilation">''[[The Old Republic: Annihilation]]''</ref> the tenuous peace brought by the Treaty of Coruscant began to collapse as a result of various proxy conflicts, Angral's campaign among them.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi" /> However, the Empire did not truly commit itself to a [[Galactic War|renewed war]] until the Emperor's hold on Revan was broken. The Force ghost of Meetra Surik enlisted the aid of the Jedi Master [[Oteg]] and an elite strike team composed of Republic soldiers and Jedi to [[Battle of the Maelstrom|free]] the imprisoned Jedi from the heart of the Maelstrom, and for the first time in centuries the Emperor was freed from Revan's mental manipulations&mdash;and no longer hindered by Revan's desire to protect the Republic. Without Revan's influence, the Emperor accelerated his plans for galactic annihilation and fueled the flames of war across the galaxy, and the Empire began to make war upon the Republic in force.<ref name="Maelstrom" /> When the Emperor learned that the former Dark Councilor [[Sajar]]&mdash;now the Padawan of Jedi Master [[Tol Braga]]&mdash;was on the planet [[Quesh]], the Emperor dispatched his Wrath to capture Sajar.<ref name="The Emperor's Wrath" />

Lord Scourge failed, however, when he encountered the Hero of Tython and recognized the Jedi as the one he had seen in his visions three hundred years ago. Knowing of the Emperor's interest in the Hero, Scourge returned empty-handed to his master and delivered the news<ref name="The Emperor's Wrath" /> that the Knight had joined a [[Jedi strike team (capture of the Sith Emperor)|strike team]] that Tol Braga was assembling&mdash;a strike team with the purpose of capturing and redeeming the Emperor.<ref name="Guided By the Force">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Guided By the Force|[[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]}}</ref> The Emperor sent a detachment of the Imperial Guard, under the command of Guardsman [[Lassicar]],<ref name="Sub-Zero Showdown">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Sub-Zero Showdown|[[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]}}</ref> to follow the Jedi to the planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], and Lassicar soon reported that the strike team intended to infiltrate the Emperor's space station.<ref name="Guided By the Force" /> On [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]], the Hero and Jedi Master [[Warren Sedoru]] had already recovered the [[Prototype cloaking device|prototype]] of the [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking device]] shielding the fortress,<ref name="Spoils of War">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Spoils of War|[[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]]}}</ref> and Lassicar's men failed in their attempts to capture the Hero and prevent the acquisition of the fortress' schematics on Hoth.<ref name="The Imperial Guard">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|The Imperial Guard|[[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]}}</ref> The Emperor also activated one of his Children, Augin Blaesus, in an attempt to kill the [[Sarkhai royal family|royal family of Sarkhai]]&mdash;an action that would have severely damaged the Republic's relationship with the [[Rift Alliance]] splinter government and harmed the Republic's war effort&mdash;but Blaesus' efforts were foiled by the Jedi Master known as the [[The Barsen'thor|Barsen'thor]].<ref name="To Serve the King" />

When the strike team landed aboard the Emperor's fortress, they were [[Mission to the Emperor's Fortress|forced to fight]] through the Imperial Guard&mdash;as well as Sithspawn known as [[Harrower assassin|Harrowers]]&mdash;to reach the Emperor, and the first Jedi to enter the Emperor's throne room were the Hero and Kira Carsen. While the Emperor watched from his throne, Scourge battled the pair in a fierce duel, but the Wrath was ultimately defeated by the two Jedi. At that moment, Braga, Sedoru, and the Jedi Knight [[Leeha Narezz]] arrived in the throne room, and Braga approached the Emperor's throne to request that he accompany the Jedi back to Tython. Leaping down from his throne, the Emperor mocked the Jedi Master for his pride and self-righteousness, surprising the strike team with his knowledge of their identities.<ref name="Descent" />

[[File:Emperor_chair.png|thumb|right|The Emperor easily overpowered Master Braga's strike team.]]
The Emperor let loose a blazing storm of violet lightning that sent Narezz and Sedoru crashing to the floor while Braga, Carsen, and the Hero struggled to deflect it. It was not long before Braga and then Carsen succumbed to the Emperor's attack as well, leaving only the Knight to advance slowly against the storm. The Emperor then summoned a ball of Force lightning in his hands and unleashed his full power against the Hero, throwing the Jedi to the floor as the Emperor began to dominate the minds of his fallen enemies. Informing them that they were now his slaves and weapons, he unleashed another blast of lightning that sent them all into [[Sleep/Legends|unconsciousness]].<ref name="Descent" />

True to his word, the Emperor bound the Jedi to his will and turned them to the dark side. His servants spent several months retraining them as Sith, transforming the fallen Jedi into the Emperor's loyal agents, and the Hero was placed under the tutelage of [[Overseer (Sith)|Overseer]] [[Chaskar]]. However, the Knight was finally freed from the Emperor's control by the spirit of Orgus Din, and the Hero escaped back to Tython with the help of Scourge. The former Emperor's Wrath revealed to the Jedi Council that the Emperor intended to complete the life-consuming ritual again on a galactic scale, but the ritual required a sacrifice of billions of simultaneous deaths to start.<ref name="An Unthinkable Alliance" /> To that end, the Emperor sent the high-ranking [[Executor (Imperial rank)|Executor]] [[Krannus]] and his [[Krannus's death cult|death cult]] to the recently discovered Republic prison world of [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]].
